security_feature_bypassed: On-zeroize invalidation of the HMAC result status, the interlock that makes HMAC512_STATUS.VALID mean that HMAC512_TAG holds an authentic engine output
finding: The zeroize arm of the hmac_core register-update block collapses the control FSM but never clears digest_valid_reg, so a security zeroize wipes the engine while leaving it advertising a valid authentication tag. The arm is a priority branch of a unique case (1'b1) statement, so the enable-gated write in the default arm is not evaluated while zeroize is asserted, and because the same arm forces the FSM to CTRL_IDLE, every later assertion of the write enable is command-guarded and never occurs. The stale bit persists indefinitely and is republished to software as HMAC512_STATUS.VALID.
detection_method: LLM-driven CSBC analysis of the audited RTL, confirmed against the file's own treatment of zeroize-sensitive state (mode_reg has its own zeroize arm at line 216, and both masked child cores clear their digest_valid_reg on the same strobe), then hardened with a 31-gate structural witness, a directed VCS simulation of hmac_core built from the project's own filelist, and a negative control in which the single missing assignment is added to the zeroize arm in a scratch copy and the identical testbench is required to fail.
security_impact: A security zeroize is the mechanism firmware uses to wipe cryptographic state before a trust-domain change. Here the wipe happens but the status does not follow: the wrapper clears its tag_valid_reg on zeroize, the next cycle reloads it from the still-set core bit, and the same transition re-fires the tag write enable after the register's hardware-clear window has closed. Software that zeroizes and then polls HMAC512_STATUS.VALID is told an authentic tag is ready when the engine has been wiped, so an all-zero value is presented as a genuine engine output. Any firmware that treats VALID as proof of authenticity, rather than re-deriving the tag, accepts a value the engine never computed.
proposed_mitigation: Add `digest_valid_reg <= 1'b0;` to the zeroize arm at src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:190-196, matching the reset arm at line 185 and the treatment mode_reg already receives at line 217.
Remove the comment at lines 192-193 that justifies the omission, since the refresh path it points at is unreachable from the idle FSM the same arm creates.
Add an assertion that digest_valid_reg is low for as long as zeroize is asserted, so any future refactor that reintroduces a deferred refresh fails in simulation rather than silently.
exploit_or_attack_flow: An HMAC operation completes, so digest_valid_reg is 1 and HMAC512_STATUS.VALID reads 1.
Privileged software writes HMAC512_CTRL.ZEROIZE, or the device enters debug-unlock or scan mode, either of which asserts the zeroize strobe at src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:259.
The zeroize arm collapses the FSM to CTRL_IDLE and the masked cores wipe their digests, but digest_valid_reg keeps its old value.

The wrapper clears tag_valid_reg for one cycle, then reloads it from the stale core bit, so HMAC512_STATUS.VALID returns to 1; the same edge re-fires the tag write enable after the hardware clear has released.
Software polls VALID, sees 1, and reads HMAC512_TAG expecting an authentic tag produced by the engine.
